title: Measure paid model and alignment costs in source-aligned lossless padding
statement: Test Bede and Thomas à Kempis, Gower and Chaucer, and Don Juan Manuel and Juan Ruiz in six linked train/test directions. Frozen training-block validation chooses order three five times and order four once. All 126 primary test packets and 24 marker-alphabet controls decode both the normalized original and the specified padded stream exactly. The source-aligned context is smaller than the output context for payload plus side bits in 4/42 matched cases. Including model and framing, the output context has the smallest complete packet of the three tested routes in all 42. It is between 2.41 and 56.58 bits per original symbol smaller than the source-aligned complete packet. The sign of their ideal loss difference changes across context orders in all 42 cases. Replacing colliding b/d markers by disjoint B/D in twelve alternating/permuted pairs preserves the arithmetic payload bit count for both predictive routes in 24/24 controlled comparisons. Changing the marker spelling changes model serialization size. Literal bd suffix padding is identical in both traversal directions. Forward decoding pays 18,488–26,520 alignment bits per 40-block packet; reverse decoding can consume each known suffix before its source word and pays zero alignment bits. The inverse route includes an enumerative index for each random marker arrangement, 12,013–12,657 bits across 40 blocks. Findings concern this finite-model family and one explicitly billed format.
check: Regenerate both models and all packets from the archived scripts and verified text cuts. Compare payload bit lengths and SHA-256 byte digests with the recorded values, and verify that source plus exact random markers are recoverable from each packet. Repeat with a less redundant model representation and independently coded work families before generalizing the cost comparison. Vary the marker schedule independently of true source boundaries and show which side information or causal codec state identifies word length when the output alphabet collides.
protocol:
# P-J-036 self-contained padding codes

Use the documented six source works, grouped in three same-language pairs
by distinct authors, with reciprocal train/test directions recorded as
linked replicates. Keep the first 64 complete ~400-character training
blocks and first 40 complete evaluation blocks per direction. Preserve
word boundaries through normalization. Hold out contiguous fit blocks
1–16, 17–32 and 33–48 for training-only order validation, using the
remaining 48 in each fold. Choose order 0–8 minimizing aggregate finite
source loss, preferring smaller order in ties. Refit each route on the
same complete 64 source-aligned training blocks. Preserve the archived
add-half state symbol base and recursive context interpolation mass two.
Report all orders' ideal test losses as descriptive sensitivity.

For constant padding use one lower-case b after each nonspace source
symbol. Alternating and permuted use the old parity of each original
letter's alphabet index (d for even, b for odd), not the parity of a
character's position. In the permuted scheme independently shuffle
each block's resulting marker multiset with three runs, training seed
10000*s+block and testing seed 10000*s+5000+block for s=1,2,3.
These replicates use the same source texts. All marker characters are
also available to the source. Interleaved state is decoder-computable
from preceding roles and whether a decoded source glyph is a space.

For suffix padding append literal bd before every word boundary, after
the letters of each word. Compare forward traversal with a transmitted
varint sequence of original word lengths and reverse traversal without
alignment side data. Forward traversal knows all spaces and emits them
as forced events for both predictive arms; exclude forced spaces from
the coded state alphabet while retaining them as context observations.
Reverse traversal reads two marker letters first and then source letters
until a decoded space. Both routes recover the same padded string.

Compare two predictive models per transform, with an identical known
source versus marker role at each event: last k output glyphs and all
output glyphs starting at the k-th most recent source event. Use the same
selected k and estimated number of symbols for the source-only inverse.
That inverse exactly regenerates deterministic padding using the declared
recipe and stores an enumerative index among arrangements for each random
marker multiset. At each block the unpadded source determines the count
of b/d. The random seed is used to produce the experimental target and
is not assumed available to the decoder.

Serialize every packet with a format tag, mode and transform, both
alphabets, order and smoothing, explicit block lengths for coded source and
original, model counts serialized canonically and compressed with zlib,
required alignment or marker bytes, and quantized arithmetic payload.
Decoder receives only packet bytes and the public implementation. Verify
exact normalized source and both raw padded bytes across each traversal.
Disclose frame overhead, model bytes, alignment and marker bytes, unpadded
arithmetic payload, padding and total. Report total bits on both original
and emitted symbol denominators, plus payload plus side bits for a shared
model comparison. This is a finite set of explicit model/format comparisons.
No Voynich text or hidden page was used.
paired_casing_protocol:
# Pure marker-alphabet comparison

For the same six directions, selected source-only order and source blocks,
repeat the alternating transform and seed-one permutation with every M-role
b/d relabeled B/D. The change makes marker letters disjoint from source
letters while preserving the exact placement, marker totals and all model
parameters. Compare the two predictive routes, with self-contained
bitstreams and separate size totals. Check exact decoding; dropping the
uppercase variants' case gives the matching colliding padded stream.
The source-only inverse cost of regenerating the spelling-case convention
is not compared in this paired control.

arith.py.source:
"""Finite-precision arithmetic coding with externally supplied CDFs.

The caller determines the decoding length and supplies the same cumulative
frequencies in the same order. Finish reports the logical bit length and
right-pads the final byte with zero bits for storage.
"""

from bisect import bisect_right

_PRECISION = 32
_FULL = 1 << _PRECISION
_MASK = _FULL - 1
_HALF = _FULL // 2
_QUARTER = _HALF // 2
_THREE_QUARTERS = _HALF + _QUARTER
_MAX_TOTAL = 1 << 16


def _total(cumulative):
    if (
        len(cumulative) < 2
        or cumulative[0] != 0
        or not 1 <= cumulative[-1] <= _MAX_TOTAL
    ):
        raise ValueError("CDF must start at zero and have total in [1, 65536]")
    if any(high <= low for low, high in zip(cumulative, cumulative[1:])):
        raise ValueError("every symbol must have positive frequency")
    return cumulative[-1]


def _restrict(low, high, cumulative, symbol, total):
    width = high - low + 1
    return (
        low + width * cumulative[symbol] // total,
        low + width * cumulative[symbol + 1] // total - 1,
    )


class Encoder:
    def __init__(self):
        self._low = 0
        self._high = _MASK
        self._pending = 0
        self._payload = bytearray()
        self._partial_byte = 0
        self._bits = 0
        self._finished = False

    def _put_bit(self, bit):
        self._partial_byte = (self._partial_byte << 1) | bit
        self._bits += 1
        if self._bits % 8 == 0:
            self._payload.append(self._partial_byte)
            self._partial_byte = 0

    def _emit(self, bit):
        self._put_bit(bit)
        for _ in range(self._pending):
            self._put_bit(1 - bit)
        self._pending = 0

    def write(self, cumulative: list[int], symbol: int):
        if self._finished:
            raise ValueError("encoder is already finished")
        total = _total(cumulative)
        if not 0 <= symbol < len(cumulative) - 1:
            raise ValueError("symbol is outside the CDF")
        low, high = _restrict(self._low, self._high, cumulative, symbol, total)
        while True:
            if high < _HALF:
                self._emit(0)
            elif low >= _HALF:
                self._emit(1)
                low -= _HALF
                high -= _HALF
            elif low >= _QUARTER and high < _THREE_QUARTERS:
                # The interval straddles the midpoint. Defer the leading bit
                # until one of the next steps moves it into a single half.
                self._pending += 1
                low -= _QUARTER
                high -= _QUARTER
            else:
                break
            low <<= 1
            high = (high << 1) | 1
        self._low, self._high = low, high

    def finish(self) -> tuple[bytes, int]:
        if self._finished:
            raise ValueError("encoder is already finished")
        self._pending += 1
        self._emit(int(self._low >= _QUARTER))
        bits_in_last_byte = self._bits % 8
        if bits_in_last_byte:
            self._payload.append(self._partial_byte << (8 - bits_in_last_byte))
        self._finished = True
        return bytes(self._payload), self._bits


class Decoder:
    def __init__(self, payload: bytes):
        self._payload = payload
        self._bit_index = 0
        self._low = 0
        self._high = _MASK
        self._code = 0
        for _ in range(_PRECISION):
            self._code = (self._code << 1) | self._get_bit()

    def _get_bit(self):
        byte_index, offset = divmod(self._bit_index, 8)
        self._bit_index += 1
        if byte_index >= len(self._payload):
            return 0
        return (self._payload[byte_index] >> (7 - offset)) & 1

    def read(self, cumulative: list[int]) -> int:
        total = _total(cumulative)
        width = self._high - self._low + 1
        point = ((self._code - self._low + 1) * total - 1) // width
        symbol = bisect_right(cumulative, point) - 1
        low, high = _restrict(self._low, self._high, cumulative, symbol, total)
        code = self._code
        while True:
            if high < _HALF:
                pass
            elif low >= _HALF:
                low -= _HALF
                high -= _HALF
                code -= _HALF
            elif low >= _QUARTER and high < _THREE_QUARTERS:
                low -= _QUARTER
                high -= _QUARTER
                code -= _QUARTER
            else:
                break
            low <<= 1
            high = (high << 1) | 1
            code = (code << 1) | self._get_bit()
        self._low, self._high, self._code = low, high, code
        return symbol


def _self_check():
    import random
    from itertools import accumulate

    rng = random.Random(8402)
    examples = [
        [],
        [([0, 1], 0)],
        [([0, 1, 2], 1)],
        [([0, 65535, 65536], 1)],
        [([0, 1, 65536], 0)] * 100,
        [([0, 1, 2, 3, 4], i % 4) for i in range(1000)],
    ]
    for length in (2, 7, 31, 32, 33, 257, 4096):
        sequence = []
        for _ in range(length):
            weights = [rng.randint(1, 1024) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 32))]
            cdf = [0, *accumulate(weights)]
            sequence.append((cdf, rng.randrange(len(weights))))
        examples.append(sequence)
    for example in examples:
        encoder = Encoder()
        for cdf, symbol in example:
            encoder.write(cdf, symbol)
        payload, bits = encoder.finish()
        assert len(payload) == (bits + 7) // 8
        if bits % 8:
            assert payload[-1] & ((1 << (8 - bits % 8)) - 1) == 0
        decoder = Decoder(payload)
        assert [decoder.read(cdf) for cdf, _ in example] == [
            symbol for _, symbol in example
        ]
    print(f"Arithmetic coder: {len(examples)} round-trip checks passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _self_check()

"""Encode and decode frozen padding comparisons on independent works."""
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path
import json
import math
import re
import sys
from zlib import ZLIB_VERSION

from codec import MARKERS, Model, SOURCE, decode, make_encoding
from padding import collect, patterns

WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
MANIFEST = json.loads((WORK / "controls/manifest.json").read_text())
CASES = [(name, seed) for name, seeds in (
    ("constant", (1,)), ("alternating", (1,)), ("permuted", (1, 2, 3)),
    ("suffix-forward", (1,)), ("suffix-reverse", (1,)),
) for seed in seeds]


def original_events(blocks):
    return [[("S", c) for c in b] for b in blocks]


def load_blocks(name):
    record = MANIFEST["works"][name]
    path = WORK / record["file"]
    raw = WORK / record["raw_file"]
    assert sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == record["sha256"]
    assert sha256(raw.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == record["raw_sha256"]
    normalized = path.read_text()
    assert re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+(?: [a-z]+)*", normalized)
    result, pieces, length = [], [], 0
    for token in normalized.split():
        pieces.append(token)
        length += len(token) + 1
        if length >= 400:
            result.append(" ".join(pieces))
            length, pieces = 0, []
    assert len(result) >= 64
    return result


def order_selection(training):
    folds = []
    for begin in range(0, 48, 16):
        end = begin + 16
        fit = training[:begin] + training[end:]
        valid = training[begin:end]
        model = Model(8, "output", {"S": SOURCE}).fit(original_events(fit))
        scores = model.ideal_path(original_events(valid))
        folds.append(scores)
        Model.prediction_path.cache_clear()
    selected = min(range(9), key=lambda order: sum(f[order] for f in folds))
    return selected, folds


def encode_mode(source, expanded, scheme, seed, train, test, order, route):
    forward = route != "inverse" and scheme == "suffix-forward"
    if route == "inverse":
        alph = {"S": SOURCE}
        fit = original_events(train)
        valid = original_events(test)
        hist = "output"
    else:
        alph = {"S": SOURCE.strip() if forward else SOURCE, "M": MARKERS}
        fit = source
        valid = expanded
        hist = route
    model = Model(8, hist, alph).fit(fit, forced_spaces=forward)
    losses = model.ideal_path(valid, forced_spaces=forward)
    selected = Model(order, hist, alph, {k: tab[:order + 1] for k, tab in model.tables.items()})
    packet, stats = make_encoding(test, expanded, selected, route, scheme)
    original, padded = decode(packet)
    expected = [collect(e, scheme)[1] for e in expanded]
    assert original == test and padded == expected
    stats["packet_sha256"] = sha256(packet).hexdigest()
    stats["ideal_bits_per_order"] = losses
    src, out = (stats["symbol_counts"][key] for key in ("original", "emitted"))
    base = stats["arithmetic_padded_bits"] + stats["side_padded_bits"]
    stats["payload_and_side_per_original"] = base / src
    stats["payload_and_side_per_emitted"] = base / out
    stats["packet_bits_per_original"] = stats["packet_bits"] / src
    stats["packet_bits_per_emitted"] = stats["packet_bits"] / out
    stats["model_and_header_fraction"] = (stats["model_bits"] + stats["header_bits"]) / stats["packet_bits"]
    if route == "inverse" and scheme == "permuted":
        stats["ideal_marker_bits"] = sum(
            math.log2(math.comb(len([c for c in b if c != " "]),
                                sum((ord(c) - ord("a")) % 2 == 0 for c in b if c != " "))) for b in test
        )
    Model.cdf.cache_clear()
    Model.prediction_path.cache_clear()
    return stats


def run_direction(pair):
    train = load_blocks(pair["train"])[:64]
    test = load_blocks(pair["test"])[:40]
    order, valid = order_selection(train)
    trials = []
    representations = {}
    for scheme, seed in CASES:
        tr = [patterns(b, scheme, seed=seed * 10000 + i) for i, b in enumerate(train)]
        te = [patterns(b, scheme, seed=seed * 10000 + 5000 + i) for i, b in enumerate(test)]
        assert all(collect(events, scheme)[0] == text for events, text in zip(tr + te, train + test))
        target_hash = sha256("\n".join(collect(xs, scheme)[1] for xs in te).encode()).hexdigest()
        representations[scheme] = target_hash
        record = {"scheme": scheme, "seed": seed, "padded_sha256": target_hash}
        for mode in ("output", "source", "inverse"):
            record[mode] = encode_mode(tr, te, scheme, seed, train, test, order, mode)
        trials.append(record)
        print(pair["pair_id"], order, scheme, seed, flush=True)
    assert representations["suffix-forward"] == representations["suffix-reverse"]
    return pair | {
        "selected_order": order,
        "validation_ideal_bits": valid,
        "train_blocks": len(train),
        "test_blocks": len(test),
        "source_sha256": sha256("\n".join(test).encode()).hexdigest(),
        "suffix_representations_equal": True,
        "trials": trials,
    }


def main():
    controls = MANIFEST["pairs"]
    requested = set(sys.argv[1:])
    results = []
    for pair in controls:
        if requested and pair["language"] not in requested:
            continue
        result = run_direction(pair)
        results.append(result)
        (WORK / f"{pair['pair_id']}.json").write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2) + "\n")
    label = "-".join(sorted(requested)) if requested else "all"
    (WORK / f"packet-results-{label}.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"results": results, "zlib": ZLIB_VERSION, "interpreter": sys.version}, indent=2
    ) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Paired disjoint marker control, with no change to source or marker locations."""
from hashlib import sha256
from pathlib import Path
import json
import runpy

from codec import Model, SOURCE, decode, make_encoding
from padding import collect, patterns

WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
main = runpy.run_path(str(WORK / "run-packets.py"))
manifest = main["MANIFEST"]
results = []
for pair in manifest["pairs"]:
    fit = main["load_blocks"](pair["train"])[:64]
    test = main["load_blocks"](pair["test"])[:40]
    order, _ = main["order_selection"](fit)
    entry = {"pair_id": pair["pair_id"], "order": order, "schemes": {}}
    for scheme in ("alternating", "permuted"):
        training = [patterns(t, scheme, 10000 + i) for i, t in enumerate(fit)]
        evaluation = [patterns(t, scheme, 15000 + i) for i, t in enumerate(test)]
        tr = [[(r, c.upper() if r == "M" else c) for r, c in row] for row in training]
        ev = [[(r, c.upper() if r == "M" else c) for r, c in row] for row in evaluation]
        expected = [collect(row, scheme)[1] for row in ev]
        assert [s.lower() for s in expected] == [collect(row, scheme)[1] for row in evaluation]
        cases = {}
        for route in ("output", "source"):
            model = Model(order, route, {"S": SOURCE, "M": "BD"}).fit(tr)
            code, stats = make_encoding(test, ev, model, route, scheme)
            assert decode(code) == (test, expected)
            cases[route] = stats | {"packet_sha256": sha256(code).hexdigest()}
            Model.cdf.cache_clear()
            Model.prediction_path.cache_clear()
        entry["schemes"][scheme] = cases
    results.append(entry)
    print(pair["pair_id"], order, flush=True)
(WORK / "collision-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2) + "\n")

"""Separate predictive payload from model, framing and side costs."""
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import json
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import mean

WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
primary = json.loads((WORK / "packet-results-all.json").read_text())
collision = json.loads((WORK / "collision-results.json").read_text())
by_case = defaultdict(list)
pairs = {}
for direction in primary["results"]:
    name = direction["pair_id"]
    rows = direction["trials"]
    assert len(rows) == 7
    pairs[name] = {}
    for case in rows:
        scheme, seed = case["scheme"], case["seed"]
        data = {route: case[route] for route in ("output", "source", "inverse")}
        for route, result in data.items():
            assert abs(result["quantized_logloss_bits"] - result["arithmetic_emitted_bits"]) < 2.1
            assert result["packet_bits"] == sum(result[k] for k in
                ("arithmetic_padded_bits", "model_bits", "header_bits", "side_padded_bits"))
        value = {
            "payload_winner": min(data, key=lambda r: data[r]["payload_and_side_per_original"]),
            "packet_winner": min(data, key=lambda r: data[r]["packet_bits"]),
            "aligned_payload_diff": data["source"]["payload_and_side_per_original"] - data["output"]["payload_and_side_per_original"],
            "aligned_packet_diff": data["source"]["packet_bits_per_original"] - data["output"]["packet_bits_per_original"],
            "source_vs_output_ideal_sign_by_order": [
                (x > y + 1e-9) - (x < y - 1e-9)
                for x, y in zip(data["source"]["ideal_bits_per_order"], data["output"]["ideal_bits_per_order"])
            ],
        }
        variable = {k: d["packet_bits"] - d["model_bits"] for k, d in data.items()}
        savings = variable["output"] - variable["source"]
        model_extra = data["source"]["model_bits"] - data["output"]["model_bits"]
        value["shared_model_break_even_packets"] = (max(1, model_extra // savings + 1)
                                                       if savings > 0 else None)
        value["forward_alignment_bits"] = data["output"]["side_bits"] if scheme == "suffix-forward" else None
        value["inverse_marker_bits"] = data["inverse"]["side_bits"] if scheme == "permuted" else None
        pairs[name][f"{scheme}.{seed}"] = value
        by_case[scheme].append(value)

def summarize(rows):
    return {
        "comparisons": len(rows),
        "payload_winner_deterministic_tiebreak": dict(Counter(r["payload_winner"] for r in rows)),
        "packet_winner": dict(Counter(r["packet_winner"] for r in rows)),
        "source_smaller_payload": sum(r["aligned_payload_diff"] < 0 for r in rows),
        "source_smaller_packet": sum(r["aligned_packet_diff"] < 0 for r in rows),
        "direction_reversal_between_payload_and_packet": sum(
            r["aligned_payload_diff"] * r["aligned_packet_diff"] < 0 for r in rows),
        "source_payload_delta_range": [
            min(r["aligned_payload_diff"] for r in rows), max(r["aligned_payload_diff"] for r in rows)
        ],
        "source_packet_delta_range": [
            min(r["aligned_packet_diff"] for r in rows), max(r["aligned_packet_diff"] for r in rows)
        ],
        "nonzero_order_rank_crossings": sum(
            -1 in r["source_vs_output_ideal_sign_by_order"] and 1 in r["source_vs_output_ideal_sign_by_order"]
            for r in rows
        ),
    }

directions = {p["pair_id"]: p for p in primary["results"]}
paired_casing = []
for d in collision:
    for scheme, disjoint in d["schemes"].items():
        colliding = next(t for t in directions[d["pair_id"]]["trials"]
                         if t["scheme"] == scheme and t["seed"] == 1)
        for mode in ("output", "source"):
            paired_casing.append({"direction": d["pair_id"], "scheme": scheme, "mode": mode,
                                  "payload_bits_colliding_minus_disjoint": colliding[mode]["arithmetic_padded_bits"]
                                  - disjoint[mode]["arithmetic_padded_bits"],
                                  "packet_bits_colliding_minus_disjoint": colliding[mode]["packet_bits"]
                                  - disjoint[mode]["packet_bits"]})

all_rows = [row for rows in by_case.values() for row in rows]
summary = {
    "primary_packets": len(all_rows) * 3,
    "case_alphabet_control_packets": len(paired_casing),
    "ordered_directions": len(primary["results"]),
    "independent_pairs": len({d["independent_pair"] for d in primary["results"]}),
    "orders": {d["pair_id"]: d["selected_order"] for d in primary["results"]},
    "per_case": {scheme: summarize(rows) for scheme, rows in by_case.items()},
    "combined": summarize(all_rows),
    "per_direction_details": pairs,
    "paired_casing": paired_casing,
}
(WORK / "packet-summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2) + "\n")

"""Prepare six independent authored text controls with known editorial boundaries."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import html
import json
import re
import shutil

from vs import refcorpus

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CONTROL = ROOT / "controls"
RAW = CONTROL / "raw"
WORKS = CONTROL / "texts"


def digest(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def checked(path: Path, sha256: str) -> str:
    data = path.read_bytes()
    if digest(data) != sha256:
        raise ValueError(f"Digest mismatch for {path.name}")
    return data.decode("utf-8-sig").replace("\r\n", "\n")


def body_paragraphs(raw: str) -> list[str]:
    start = re.search(r"<body\b[^>]*>", raw, flags=re.I)
    if not start:
        raise ValueError("Missing HTML body")
    main = raw[start.end():]
    end = re.search(r"<table\b", main, flags=re.I)
    if not end:
        raise ValueError("Missing expected navigation table")
    return [
        html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]*>", "", part)).strip()
        for part in re.findall(r"<p\b[^>]*>(.*?)</p\s*>", main[:end.start()], flags=re.I | re.S)
    ]


def bede(raw: str) -> str:
    parts = body_paragraphs(raw)
    start = next(i for i, paragraph in enumerate(parts) if re.match(r"^\[1\]\s+Brittania", paragraph))
    return "\n".join(parts[start:])


def kempis(raw: str) -> str:
    return "\n".join(part for part in body_paragraphs(raw) if re.match(r"^\d+\.\s", part))


def gower(raw: str) -> str:
    start = raw.index("Incipit Liber Primus")
    end = raw.index("Explicit Liber Primus", start)
    body = raw[start:end]
    start_of_verse = re.search(r"(?m)^I may noght strecche up to the hevene\s*$", body)
    if not start_of_verse or "_" in body[start_of_verse.start():]:
        raise ValueError("Unexpected presentation of Gower's first book")
    return body[start_of_verse.start():]


def chaucer(raw: str) -> str:
    start = raw.index("WHILOM*, as olde stories tellen us,")
    end = raw.index("Notes to The Knight’s Tale.", start)
    lines = raw[start:end].splitlines()
    left_column = [re.split(r" {5,}| {2,}(?=\*)", line.strip(), maxsplit=1)[0] for line in lines]
    return re.sub(r"<[^>\n]+>", "", "\n".join(left_column))


def juan_manuel(raw: str) -> str:
    heading = re.compile(r"(?m)^E(?:NX|X|NJ|J)EMPLO ([IVXLCDM]+)[ \t]*$")
    starts = list(heading.finditer(raw))
    labels = ("I", "II", "III", "IV", "V", "VI", "VII", "VIII", "IX", "X", "XI")
    start = next(i for i, match in enumerate(starts) if match[1] == "I")
    stories = starts[start:start + len(labels)]
    if tuple(match[1] for match in stories) != labels:
        raise ValueError("Missing consecutive examples I–XI")
    main_parts = []
    for head, after in zip(stories, stories[1:]):
        story = raw[head.end():after.start()].strip("\n")
        layout = re.split(r"\n[ \t]*\n", story, maxsplit=1)
        if len(layout) != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"Missing separation from the example {head[1]} caption")
        prose = layout[1]
        editorial = re.search(r"(?m)^ {2,}\[\d+\]", prose)
        if not editorial:
            raise ValueError(f"No dedicated endnote separator for example {head[1]}")
        main_parts.append(re.sub(r"\[\d+\]", "", prose[:editorial.start()]))
    return "\n".join(main_parts)


def juan_ruiz(raw: str) -> str:
    start = re.search(r"(?m)^892 Dueñas,", raw)
    if not start:
        raise ValueError("Missing start of stanza 892")
    body = raw[start.start():]
    stop = re.search(r"(?m)^1100 Como avía", body)
    if not stop:
        raise ValueError("Missing start of stanza 1100")
    verse = re.sub(r"\{\d+\}|\[[A-Z]\]", "", body[:stop.start()])
    return "\n".join(line for line in verse.splitlines() if not line.strip().isupper())


def counted_blocks(normalized: str) -> int:
    complete = 0
    chars = 0
    for word in normalized.split():
        chars += len(word) + 1
        if chars >= 400:
            complete += 1
            chars = 0
    return complete


def prepare(previous: Path, pinned: Path) -> None:
    WORKS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    previous_sources = json.loads((previous / "external-texts.json").read_text())
    pins = {entry["id"]: entry for entry in refcorpus.pins()}
    specs = [
        ("latin_bede", "latin", "Bede", "Historia ecclesiastica gentis Anglorum, Book I",
         "731", "ecclesiastical history", "bede.html", bede, previous_sources["bede_historia_i"],
         "HTML paragraphs from the chapter 1 Brittania paragraph to the navigation footer."),
        ("latin_kempis", "latin", "Thomas à Kempis (traditional attribution)",
         "De imitatione Christi, Book I", "15th century", "devotional prose",
         "kempis.html", kempis, previous_sources["kempis_imitatio_i"],
         "Numbered HTML prose paragraphs of Book I, excluding chapter headings, navigation and footer."),
        ("english_gower", "english", "John Gower", "Confessio Amantis, Book I",
         "late 14th century", "narrative verse", "gower-266.txt", gower,
         {"url": "https://gutenberg.pglaf.org/2/6/266/266-0.txt",
          "catalog_url": "https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/266",
          "raw_sha256": "7ec852c556d9a0f44ad32fcf2de4d55f0256dd1354fa2448b00d5bff3d5ed3fe",
          "edition": "Project Gutenberg eBook #266, based on Macaulay"},
         "English verse beginning I may noght strecche, after the italic Latin stanza, through the line before Explicit Liber Primus. Line numbers disappear under normalization."),
        ("english_chaucer", "english", "Geoffrey Chaucer", "The Knight’s Tale",
         "late 14th century", "narrative verse", "chaucer-2383.txt", chaucer, pins["en_chaucer"],
         "Knight’s Tale left-column verse from WHILOM to Notes to The Knight’s Tale; remove right-column glosses at strings of five spaces or at two spaces before asterisk and strip angle-bracket note markers. Purves edition with some modernized spelling."),
        ("spanish_lucanor", "spanish", "Don Juan Manuel", "El conde Lucanor, Examples I–X",
         "c. 1335", "prose exempla", "lucanor-65738.txt", juan_manuel, pins["es_lucanor"],
         "Use the body of each of Examples I–X between the title paragraph and the first dedicated numbered editorial note; strip inline note numbers."),
        ("spanish_buenamor", "spanish", "Juan Ruiz", "Libro de Buen Amor, stanzas 892–1099",
         "14th century", "narrative and religious verse", "buenamor-16625.txt", juan_ruiz,
         pins["es_buenamor"],
         "Verses beginning 892 Dueñas and stopping before stanza 1100, from Cejador y Frauca’s 1913 second volume. Remove numbered page braces, bracketed editorial marker letters and standalone uppercase section headings."),
    ]

    manifest = {"works": {}, "pairs": [], "window": {
        "minimum_training_blocks": 64,
        "minimum_evaluation_blocks": 40,
        "approximate_block_characters": 400,
        "boundary": "Complete words with canonical single spaces. Counts below are full blocks only.",
    }}
    for key, lang, author, title, date, genre, filename, clean, meta, boundary in specs:
        target_raw = RAW / filename
        if "raw_file" in meta:
            shutil.copyfile(previous / meta["raw_file"], target_raw)
        elif "file" in meta:
            shutil.copyfile(pinned / meta["file"], target_raw)
        raw_sha = meta.get("raw_sha256", meta.get("sha256"))
        normalized = refcorpus.normalize(clean(checked(target_raw, raw_sha)), lang)
        if counted_blocks(normalized) < 64:
            raise ValueError(f"Too few complete blocks for {key}")
        target = WORKS / f"{key}.txt"
        target.write_bytes(normalized.encode("ascii"))
        manifest["works"][key] = {
            "language": lang,
            "author": author,
            "title": title,
            "date": date,
            "genre": genre,
            "url": meta["url"],
            "edition": meta.get("edition", f"Pinned Project Gutenberg release {meta.get('id', '')}"),
            "source_notes": meta.get("license", "Source distributed by Project Gutenberg."),
            "catalog_url": meta.get("catalog_url"),
            "pin_id": meta.get("id"),
            "body_boundary": boundary,
            "raw_file": str(target_raw.relative_to(ROOT)),
            "raw_sha256": raw_sha,
            "file": str(target.relative_to(ROOT)),
            "sha256": digest(target.read_bytes()),
            "characters_including_spaces": len(normalized),
            "words": len(normalized.split()),
            "complete_blocks_at_400": counted_blocks(normalized),
        }
    for a, b in (("latin_bede", "latin_kempis"), ("english_gower", "english_chaucer"),
                 ("spanish_lucanor", "spanish_buenamor")):
        for train, test in ((a, b), (b, a)):
            manifest["pairs"].append({
                "pair_id": f"{train}_to_{test}", "train": train, "test": test,
                "language": manifest["works"][train]["language"],
                "independent_pair": f"{a}__{b}",
            })
    manifest["normalization"] = "Use pinned vs.refcorpus.normalize on the isolated body for each language. Output UTF-8 ASCII, single symbolic spaces, no terminal newline."
    manifest["paired_design"] = "Two orientations per language pair, with separate work-level train and test. The orientations reuse the same two works and must not count as independent samples."
    (CONTROL / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("previous_controls", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("pinned_repository", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    prepare(args.previous_controls, args.pinned_repository)
